If sentiment is positive in the last 3 days and forecast is trending up, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days).  
If sentiment is negative in the last 3 days and forecast is trending down, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days).  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is flat, apply a 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment for late horizon (16–30 days) to capture momentum.  
When sentiment swings from negative to positive over 3 days, shift forecast peak 2–3 days earlier and increase amplitude by 1–2%.  
If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, suppress forecast overshoots by 2–3% in late horizon to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, apply a 2–3% downward bias to forecast mid horizon to reflect bearish sentiment persistence.
